Designing useful underwater thrust

Our team needed a ducted thruster we could fabricate and fit into the ROV.

As mechanical design lead, I developed the ducted propeller and thruster assembly in SolidWorks and studied the flow with Flow Simulation. I worked with the electrical team on prototype integration and helped teammates with the CFD setup, assembly, and testing.

Comparing the flow in simulation

I used a duct and rotating-region model to examine the flow around the propeller. The velocity trajectories helped me explain the flow through the duct and compare possible revisions with teammates.

Thrust and momentum flow
T ≈ ṁ(vout − vin)

This simplified momentum balance relates thrust to the change in flow velocity. It omits pressure and other control-volume terms, so geometry, rotational speed, and test conditions still matter.

Building and testing the thruster

The prototype produced approximately 10 N of thrust in project testing.

I helped teammates work through manufacturing and installation details, coordinate the mechanical and electrical interfaces, and prepare the assembly for testing.
